title: Maximum-Entropy Random Walks on Hypergraphs
summary: Random walks are fundamental tools for analyzing complex networked systems, including social networks, biological systems, and communication infrastructures. While classical random walks focus on pairwise interactions, many real-world systems exhibit higher-order interactions naturally modeled by hypergraphs. Existing random walk models on hypergraphs often focus on undirected structures or do not incorporate entropy-based inference, limiting their ability to capture directional flows, uncertainty, or information diffusion in complex systems.
